text:
maya: Heads-up: I'm prototyping a 'wavefront weighting' prefetched warmup refactor for safetensors-sharded bundles. Goal: smooth out mem spikes during model hotstart and prioritize small active layers first so short-context requests get sub-100ms tail latency.

liam: high-level idea?

maya: wavefront = ordering layers by runtime activation importance (attention layers that are hot for short seqs -> earlier). We assign weights per-layer from profile heatmaps and drive prefetch budget scheduler.

sasha: sounds promising. how do you compute "importance"? expensive profiling?

maya: cheap heuristics + sampled traces. Start with static heuristics (layer type + param count + position) and refine with live telemetry buckets. lightweight offline job to produce layer weights per-model-version.

aj: compatibility with existing shard manifests? we can't change wire format mid-deploy.

maya: no wire changes. It's a runtime-only scheduler that reads an optional companion .layerweights file alongside manifest. If missing, falls back to round-robin/hotstart we have today.

liam: risk: biasing towards small layers could starve big layers and cause KV cache thrash later.

maya: agreed. my plan: soft-weights + progressive windowing. we ensure every layer gets at least minimal warmfill before marking done. Also enforce eviction-safe thresholds.

prefetch-bot: perf-sim job queued: model=redwood-7B-dev, profile-sample=2000, seed=17

liam: what's the migration path for Dedicated fleets? need rollout strategy and a graceful rollback.

maya: can be gated via rollout flag per-cluster. Console will expose an opt-in. We also add an A/B metric: cold-start tail percentile and peak memory. Rollback is simply disabling the scheduler (runtime fallback).

sasha: what about multi-format bundles (safetensors + quant sidecar)? We can't assume contiguous layout.

maya: we operate at layer logical level using manifest offsets. For quant sidecars we treat them as distinct weight sources but map to same layer id. Prefetch reads are abstracted through weightsource API, unchanged.

aj: telemetry - what signals do we need to trust this?

maya: 1) per-layer first-use latency, 2) bytes-read-by-layer during first N requests, 3) memory peak over warm period, 4) request latency percentiles. We'll add a lightweight shim that tags warmup reads with traceable marker.

liam: any concern about state explosion in metadata (layerweights files for every model-version)?

maya: keep it compact (text proto ~1KB per model), stored in model catalog alongside manifest. We only generate for curated subset initially.

sasha: perf expectation? numbers?

maya: early sim looked like 20-40% reduction in 95/99 tail for short-response workloads and 10-15% lower peak memory on p3-like instances. Real numbers will vary.

aj: implementation plan and owners?

maya: plan: (1) weightspec companion reader + scheduler (PR1, me) (2) telemetry tags + offline job to generate initial weights (PR2, sasha) (3) console flag + rollout hooks (PR3, liam) (4) canary on dev fleet (team eng-ml). Target: 3 sprints.

liam: blockers?

maya: integration testing for eviction behavior and cross-shard prefetch ordering. Also need a small contract for the companion file format. I'll draft RFC follow-up for that contract.

prefetch-bot: canary job scheduled: fleet=dev-wavefront-canary, start=1837774600

aj: please add a small experiment to compare with existing random-prefetch baseline. put results in the perf dash.

maya: will do. I'll post the RFC follow-up and attach simulation logs here. Thanks! :thumbsup:
